Global praise for HK infrastructure
body:
InfraEX Week 2026 opened yesterday with its flagship event – the 2nd International Infrastructure and Projects Leaders Summit – bringing together leading experts and professionals from over 30 countries and regions.

 

Participants praised the summit’s strong global appeal and shared positive views on Hong Kong’s ongoing infrastructure development.

 

Ashghal Technical Office Assistant Manager Hayat Bukshaisha said that Hong Kong has strong experience in planning and delivering major infrastructure projects.

 

“We are taking Hong Kong as a benchmark. We look to Hong Kong and learn from past experience, especially when it comes to modern methods of construction and project delivery,” she said.

 

Deloitte Australia Senior Partner Sean McClowry noted that he is particularly interested in the Northern Metropolis Project.

 

“It is one of the most exciting initiatives of its kind in the world, and seeing this kind of greenfield initiative coming to life is really exciting for me,” he said. “Always when I come to Hong Kong, just seeing how the infrastructure works together and how you fuse physical infrastructure and digital technologies is very interesting to me.”

 

Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Singapore Executive Director (Centre for Public Project Management) Low Chian Siong highlighted the value of opportunities that he gained by joining the event.

 

“The greatest takeaway for me is not just learning what other participants are doing, but also actually the network that we create and continue to maintain,” he said.

 

He said he was also amazed by how much Hong Kong has achieved in a very short time in terms of planning and execution.

 

Meanwhile, Professor Tarek Zayed of The Hong Kong Polytechnic University Department of Construction Management & Intelligence, who has spent nine years working in Hong Kong, emphasised the city’s high standards in infrastructure.

 

“I have been in contact with many departments in Hong Kong and doing a lot of research in many infrastructures including bridges, tunnels, water networks, sewer networks, highways or pavement. The infrastructure here is strong, very good, and many of them are new, very sustainable and resilient for the coming generation.”

 

Association of Consulting Engineers of Hong Kong Chairman Ole Wong said that the summit encourages valuable exchanges with overseas professionals.

 

“We can share, we can collaborate and we think about an integrated opportunity with each other together. So the summit is very successful and we hope we can meet as many leaders as possible from different places. We can all work together and we can think about our future, embrace our challenges together,” he said.

title: InfraEX Week 2026 opens
body:
InfraEX Week 2026, spearheaded by the Development Bureau, opened today.

 

The event aims to establish a premier international exchange platform to promote sustainable development, enhance infrastructure delivery efficiency and accelerate the adoption of innovative technologies. It serves as a key catalyst to modernise and transform the construction industry.

 

Speaking at the grand opening ceremony, Chief Executive John Lee said that in a world shaped by shifting geopolitics, urgent climate challenges and rapid technological advance, ideas must be turned into lasting projects through innovation, collaboration and clear strategic direction.

 

He added that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan provides a vital roadmap for the future, giving businesses, investors and innovators clear insight into the city's development and emerging opportunities. He cited the Northern Metropolis, which is central to the Plan, as a prime example of these opportunities.

 

To build the Northern Metropolis and all that it promises, Mr Lee said Hong Kong must deliver future-ready infrastructure supported by smart city concepts, artificial intelligence, advanced engineering technologies and innovative construction methods and materials. He stressed that collaboration is the most crucial factor for achieving excellence in the construction industry.

     

Mr Lee then witnessed the exchange of a letter of intent and memoranda of understanding between the Development Bureau and various local and overseas institutions. These agreements will foster deeper cross-regional and cross-sectoral collaboration, laying a solid foundation for more local and Mainland construction enterprises and products to go global.

     

Vice Minister of the Ministry of Water Resources Liu Dongshun noted at the ceremony that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government announced its First Five-Year Plan in September this year, outlining goals to advance the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA), strengthen physical infrastructure connectivity and boost digitalisation and infrastructure resilience. He added that Hong Kong is leveraging its unique advantage of strong national support alongside close global connections to reinforce its position as an international infrastructure hub.

 

He stressed that the Ministry of Water Resources will deepen exchanges and co-operation with Hong Kong on water-related affairs, providing reliable water security to support the GBA’s high-quality development and safeguard the city’s long-term prosperity and stability.

      

The Week features three major construction events: its flagship opening event, the 2nd International Infrastructure & Projects Leaders Summit, alongside the International Conference on Modular Construction 2026 and the Construction Innovation Expo 2026.     

 

Held concurrently today, the 2nd International Infrastructure & Projects Leaders Summit is themed “Envisioning a Sustainable Future: From Insights to Impacts”. It explored strategies to tackle industry challenges while driving the sector’s modernisation and high-quality growth.

     

In her welcome remarks at the Summit luncheon, Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said that under “one country, two systems”, Hong Kong proactively integrates into and serves national development. She added that the city remains committed to its role as a “super-connector” and “super value-adder” to help internationalise national standards and showcase the nation’s innovation and technology to the world.

 

She noted that the Government is steering the construction industry towards advanced, intelligent and high-quality growth. While accelerating the Northern Metropolis development, the Government is overhauling practices across the board, harnessing artificial intelligence and promoting the widespread adoption of advanced construction materials and technologies.

     

Permanent Secretary for Development (Works) Ricky Lau said in his keynote presentation at the Summit that the Government is accelerating the Northern Metropolis and other major infrastructure projects, creating vast opportunities for the construction industry.

 

He noted that as the industry navigates rapid technological shifts, infrastructure upgrades and climate resilience, it is transitioning from traditional delivery models towards a more industrialised, digitalised and tech-enabled phase. This transformation will be driven by three core pillars – innovation, talent development and collaboration – enabling the industry to move forward.

     

Over 800 major infrastructure project leaders and experts from more than 30 countries and regions attended the Summit, including senior Mainland and overseas government officials as well as representatives from renowned organisations such as the International Institute for Management Development. They shared the latest infrastructure initiatives and challenges at the presentation session and four plenary sessions.

title: NM ordinance published in Gazette
body:
The Northern Metropolis (NM) Development Ordinance was published in the Gazette today, providing the legal basis for facilitation measures that cover town planning, land compensation, building works approvals, noise control, and cross-boundary flows.

 

The NM will be developed to serve as a hub for higher education, innovation and technology, while offering an environment suitable for living, working and travelling.

 

It will act as the main platform for Hong Kong to deeply engage in the development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and to actively integrate into and serve overall national development, while serving as a strategic engine to foster economic transformation and develop new quality productive forces.

 

Passed by the Legislative Council at its third reading on November 12, the ordinance carries great significance for Hong Kong in proactively aligning with the National 15th Five-Year Plan and implementing Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan.

 

The ordinance aims to expedite development and construction, while helping enterprises establish a presence in the NM.

 

The Development Bureau and relevant bureaus are formulating the first batch of subsidiary legislation needed to implement these facilitation measures, with a view to tabling it for LegCo's vetting in January and bringing it into effect in the first quarter of 2027.

 

Pursuant to the provisions of the ordinance that have come into operation, the Secretary for Development has published the plan delineating the NM area on the website. A copy has also been made available at the office of the Land Registry for public inspection.

title: Stepping up maritime hub push
body:
Secretary for Transport & Logistics Mable Chan has outlined how Hong Kong is upgrading and transforming its shipping industry to build a global maritime hub, aligning the city’s First Five-Year Plan with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. Highlighting Hong Kong’s role as the strategic southern gateway linking the Mainland with the world, she noted that the city serves as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder".

 

To consolidate and enhance Hong Kong’s status as an international shipping centre, the Government is adopting a dual-core strategy that boosts port competitiveness while fostering a vibrant, high-value maritime services cluster. Ms Chan expected that these efforts will strengthen the city’s resilience and attract fresh business opportunities for the sector.

 

"They can finance, they can build and also lead from Hong Kong as the base, to enter into a more rigorous and more complete holistic development of maritime and shipping development for Hong Kong," she said.

 

One of the key measures to enhance port competitiveness is the green transformation of the maritime industry. Hong Kong is the seventh-largest bunkering hub globally by volume, having completed over 210 green maritime fuel bunkering operations totalling more than 370,000 tonnes from January 2025 through the third quarter of 2026.

 

Ms Chan noted that Hong Kong holds strong potential to become a leading Green Maritime Fuel Bunkering & Trade Centre. To advance this goal, the Government has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Zhanjiang in Guangdong to jointly establish Hong Kong’s very first Green Energy Corridor.

 

Ms Chan added that the Government will collaborate with relevant parties to develop national and international standards and certification systems for green shipping fuel. It will also leverage Hong Kong’s mature capital-raising platform to finance investments in green fuel shipping.

title: FS to visit UK and Netherlands
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan will depart for a visit to the United Kingdom and the Netherlands late tonight.

 

He will lead a delegation of over 20 members, comprising representatives of various government departments, public organisations and industry bodies, as well as leaders from the investment and innovation and technology (I&T) sectors, to enhance business and I&T exchanges between Hong Kong and the two places, promote opportunites in Hong Kong, and foster investment and collaboration.

 

During their visit to the UK from November 22 to 25, the delegation will visit the University of Cambridge and attend a dialogue on innovation co-organised by the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC) and the university.

 

They will also visit the university's innovation commercialisation arm and the research and development centre of a biopharmaceutical company. In London, they will attend the plenary session of the Hong Kong-Europe Business Council, a lunch hosted by the Hong Kong Association, and a Hong Kong Dinner organised by the HKTDC.

 

Mr Chan will also meet with local business, financial and think tank leaders, and attend a financial sector roundtable while in the UK capital.

 

During their visit to the Netherlands from November 25 to 28, the delegation will stop in Amsterdam, The Hague and Eindhoven to visit various I&T companies, parks and hubs. They will also participate in a number of business lunches to brief various sectors of the local community on developments in Hong Kong.

 

In addition, Mr Chan will meet local political, business, financial and think tank leaders, and attend a number of roundtable meetings and exchange sessions.

 

He will arrive back in Hong Kong on the morning of November 29. During his absence, Deputy Financial Secretary Michael Wong will be Acting Financial Secretary.

title: AI risk working group convenes
body:
Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today convened the first meeting of the Working Group on Coordination of AI Risk Governance to comprehensively advance implementation of the policy strategy.

 

Noting that while artificial intelligence (AI) is developing rapidly, promoting industry upgrades, and improving everyday convenience, Mr Chan stressed that managing its impact across society and prioritising risk governance and application safety are equally crucial.

 

He said the working group will steer and co-ordinate the efforts of bureaux and departments to examine issues relating to AI development risks, governance, and safety; strengthen public awareness; and develop corresponding management and regulatory frameworks. This aims to ensure that while accelerating technological adoption, these tools are used for good and remain safe and under control.

 

At the meeting, the working group reviewed and co-ordinated the work plans and implementation proposals for the seven specific actions under the AI risk governance strategy. These cover combating the use of AI in criminal activities, enhancing the protection of minor users, promoting market assessment of ethical issues, ensuring the safe and orderly application of the technology across industries, examining legal liability arising from accidents caused by automated products, introducing guidelines on agent management, and evaluating the impact of automation on employment.

 

To ensure that Hong Kong's AI risk governance strategy is implemented comprehensively, soundly, and in an orderly manner, the working group will convene regularly as work advances to review and oversee departmental execution of the various measures, and facilitate interdepartmental collaboration.

title: 20th ICT Awards honours winners
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan today presented the Award of the Year at the Hong Kong ICT Awards 2026 ceremony to a joint team of government departments and local organisations.

 

The winning team comprises the Electrical & Mechanical Services Department, the Architectural Services Department, the Housing Department, the Hong Kong Center for Construction Robotics Limited and the Hong Kong Housing Society, which also won the Smart Business Grand Award for its AI-enabled Smart Water Tank Cleaning Robot.

 

Secretary for Innovation, Technology & Industry Prof Sun Dong presented trophies to the eight winners of Grand Awards at the ceremony to recognise their outstanding performance.

 

Addressing the ceremony, Mr Chan said: “Look back at the winners over the years and you can see how much has changed. The technology has changed. But the winners have something in common: they saw what people needed and found a new way to help.”

     

Mr Chan noted that some of the most important applications of artificial intelligence (AI) may still lie ahead. “AI can help us do familiar things better. The more interesting question is: what may it allow us to do differently? Many of the winners tonight are pointing the way. They show us not just what AI can do, but what it makes possible for people,” he said.

     

He added that the Government’s role is to give innovators the conditions to succeed, noting that the Committee on AI+ & Industry Development Strategy is helping more industries put AI to work. Mr Chan also highlighted that the data facility cluster being built at Sandy Ridge will expand Hong Kong’s computing capacity, while the Hong Kong AI Research & Development Institute will help turn research breakthroughs into practical applications.

 

In addition, the Government is training specialists and rolling out its AI for All programme to help people across the community use AI with confidence.

 

Established in 2006 and celebrating its 20th anniversary this year, the annual Hong Kong ICT Awards have tracked the innovation and growth of the city’s tech sector. The awards continue to honour outstanding enterprises and talent in ICT innovation, encouraging the industry to pursue excellence.

title: HK IP Academy launches
body:
Financial Secretary Paul Chan today attended the opening ceremony of the 16th Business of Intellectual Property (IP) Asia Forum, during which the Hong Kong Intellectual Property Academy was officially launched.

 

A major IP conference, the forum is being held over two days at the Convention & Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai.

 

Speaking at the forum, Mr Chan said the National 15th Five-Year Plan supports Hong Kong in deepening its development as a regional IP trading centre.

 

Launched in partnership with the Monetary Authority last December, the IP Financing Sandbox has so far seen banks approve seven loans.

 

Mr Chan highlighted that the task now is to move from "sandbox to scale".

 

“Banks, valuers and borrowers are discovering together what makes IP bankable," he said. "The next phase of the initiative will draw in more participants. And a new pilot scheme will help smaller firms obtain professional valuations of their patents, in line with the national standard.

 

“An agreement is only as reliable as its enforcement, so IP disputes can be settled here in Hong Kong by arbitration or mediation, under a bilingual common law system that international parties know well.”

 

The Hong Kong Intellectual Property Academy was jointly established by the Intellectual Property Department and the Vocational Training Council.

 

The Government earmarked $52 million in the 2026-27 Budget to support the academy's establishment and its first two years of operation. It is expected to provide training for around 2,000 participants over the two-year pilot period.

 

Speaking at the academy’s opening ceremony, Acting Secretary for Commerce & Economic Development Bernard Chan remarked that Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan sets out the establishment of an IP academy to systematically nurture talent for IP-intensive industries, equipping practitioners with knowledge and skills spanning IP creation, protection, management, financing, utilisation and commercialisation.

 

To support innovation and technology, as well as the business, professional services, cultural and creative sectors, the academy will establish a multilevel on-the-job training pathway, and develop certified courses and Qualifications Framework-recognised programmes.

 

The academy's first foundation course is being held today and tomorrow during the forum.

title: CE hails 5 APEC Summit outcomes
body:
Chief Executive John Lee said today that Hong Kong achieved five major outcomes during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit held in Shenzhen, ranging from strengthened ties with Southeast Asian nations to new agreements with emerging markets.

 

Speaking to the media this afternoon, Mr Lee emphasised Hong Kong's active role in supporting China's hosting of the regional forum.

 

“First, contributing Hong Kong's strength by actively participating in and supporting our country's successful hosting of the APEC meeting," said Mr Lee, noting that the city organised meetings and workshops while launching a series of capacity-building projects throughout the event.

 

During the summit, Mr Lee focused on bilateral diplomacy to deepen exchanges with fellow APEC economies and consolidate ties with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN).

 

“I met with the leaders of seven economies – Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei, Thailand, Chile, Peru and Singapore – to strengthen ties and discuss issues of mutual concern,” he said. “The APEC meetings provided me with the opportunity to meet with five ASEAN leaders at bilateral meetings and engagements to further consolidate our relations.”

 

In a move to expand the city's reach into emerging markets, Mr Lee pointed to a new bilateral milestone reached on Wednesday.

 

"Yesterday, the President of Chile and I jointly witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme Agreement between Hong Kong and Chile," he said.

 

Rounding out the achievements, Mr Lee highlighted his efforts at Tuesday’s CEO Summit to promote the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) and showcase Hong Kong’s unique advantages to international business and political leaders.

 

The Chief Executive added that Hong Kong has been making efforts to deepen the city's integration into national development.

 

“I think we can deepen Greater Bay Area development through hard, soft and heart connectivity and take forward the Northern Metropolis for integrating into national development. Second, we can contribute to Belt & Road co-operation.

 

“Third, we can, through the Go Global Task Force, support many enterprises in leveraging Hong Kong's world-class professional services and extensive global network, in using Hong Kong as a springboard to expand into global markets.”

title: APEC CEO Summit opens
body:
Chief Executive John Lee attended the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit in Shenzhen today and met leaders of other economies during the day.

 

President Xi Jinping delivered a keynote speech at the opening ceremony, pointing out that APEC was born amid the waves of economic globalisation and enabled the Asia-Pacific to steer the course of the times. Noting that this year marks the third time China has hosted APEC, he said that China is ready to work with all parties to forge ahead with resolve, jointly build an Asia-Pacific community and bring prosperity for all in the region.

 

President Xi put forward four proposals: to uphold peace and stability, to build bridges of opening up and co-operation, to boost innovation to drive growth and to expand ways for mutual benefits and win-win outcomes. He also said China supports establishing a World Association for Bay Areas Economic Cooperation to deepen exchanges among bay areas worldwide and explore new ways for stronger regional economic co-operation.

 

Mr Lee said he was deeply encouraged and inspired by President Xi's keynote speech, noting that from a strategic and long-term perspective, it charted the course for Asia-Pacific co-operation. He added that the speech underscored the need to firmly uphold the post-war international order, resolve differences through dialogue and negotiation and respond to challenges through solidarity and collaboration to lay a solid foundation for long-term regional peace and stability.

 

The Chief Executive highlighted that as an APEC member economy, Hong Kong has long served as an important hub for regional economic and trade co-operation and is one of the world's most competitive economies. He noted that Hong Kong has consistently supported free trade and multilateralism, actively leveraging the APEC platform to continuously deepen international exchanges and co-operation.

 

Afterwards, Mr Lee met Malaysia's Prime Minister Dato' Seri Anwar Ibrahim and noted that the official opening of the Hong Kong Economic & Trade Office in Kuala Lumpur is deepening ties and investment promotion with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and neighbouring Asian countries. Highlighting Hong Kong's development as an international hub for high-calibre talent and a Muslim-friendly destination, Mr Lee welcomed more Malaysian students and visitors to Hong Kong.

 

Mr Lee then met Vietnam's President To Lam, noting that the two places share a vision for promoting high-quality development. He encouraged Vietnamese enterprises to leverage Hong Kong's advantages in connecting the Mainland and the world, using the city as a springboard to tap into the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and seize more opportunities together.

 

In the afternoon, Mr Lee met Brunei's Sultan Haji Hassanal Bolkiah. Mr Lee said that Hong Kong's world-class capital markets, professional services and aviation and logistics network can strongly support deeper co-operation, expressing hope that both sides will further strengthen collaboration and complement each other's strengths.

 

In addition, Mr Lee met Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, noting that Thailand is developing its innovation and technology industries while Hong Kong is advancing the integrated development of education, technology and talent. He expressed hope that the two places would strengthen connectivity and co-operation in innovation and technology, encouraging more Thai enterprises to establish a presence in Hong Kong to expand into international markets.

 

Mr Lee then met Chile's President José Antonio Kast and witnessed the signing of the Working Holiday Scheme agreement between Hong Kong and Chile. Mr Lee said Hong Kong will continue to leverage its roles as a "super-connector" and "super value-adder" to strengthen bilateral co-operation in different areas.

 

Mr Lee thanked the leaders of Malaysia, Vietnam, Brunei and Thailand for their continued support for Hong Kong's early accession to the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and the joint promotion of regional economic development. He added that amid a complex and ever-changing international landscape, Hong Kong is actively expanding into diversified markets and deepening collaboration with ASEAN, Latin America and other countries of the Global South.

 

In the evening, Mr Lee was due to attend a welcome banquet for leaders and representatives of the participating economies. Tomorrow, he will attend the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting and hold bilateral talks with other regional leaders.
